name: Black Feathered Snake
reason: The source creature name 'Black Feathered Snake' was carried over unchanged, as the literal English term already fits the Western fantasy register.
description: A small, glossy black snake with a feather-like crest found in the marsh (Eps 702-707). Its venom is legendary in the Heartlands - fast, total, and without antidote - and Zane famously takes its bite without flinching during the marsh escape with Cora.

name: Orange-Tooth Crocodiles
reason: Source beast species 'Orange-toothed Crocodile' (ch 684) was kept nearly verbatim, lightly restyled as 'Orange-Tooth Crocodile'.
description: A crocodile species of the marsh waters (Ep 704) with rows of orange-red teeth; in the source these beasts pose no real threat to the protagonist and are avoided rather than hunted by warriors.

name: Water Serpent
reason: The source creature term 'Water Serpent' (ch ~685) was carried over unchanged.
description: A powerful marsh creature near the underground palace (Ep 706) that killed a Spirit-Tribulation warrior who strayed into its territory, drawing Maddox's interest - mirroring the source scene where Cui Xie's interest is piqued by the Water Serpent.

name: Coupled Cultivation
reason: The source term 'dual cultivation' (chs 687-688, 940) was renamed 'Coupled Cultivation' to soften the term for the adaptation's register.
description: A class of paired cultivation methods regarded as a forbidden path in the Heartlands but openly practiced in the upper world (Lavender mentions secret Coupled Cultivation methods, Ep 708; Leah Jones's Siren's Kiss Sect teaches them, Ep 967).

name: Heaven Sword
reason: The source technique 'Heavenly Sword' (whose 'Sword Eye' lets the user absorb the Force of the Heavens into the blade) was localized as 'Heaven Sword'.
description: Finn's signature sword technique (Eps 711, 995). Its higher level, the Sword Eye, channels Heaven's Force directly into the blade and stores it as pure sword intent - a single charged strike can kill a Life-and-Death Realm warrior, at great physical cost to the wielder. Corresponds to Hua Tianming's Sword Eye of the Heavenly Sword in the source.

name: Heaven-grade
reason: The source talent classification 'Heaven Grade' (e.g. 'Heaven Grade geniuses') was kept with hyphenated styling.
description: A talent classification for exceptional geniuses (Eps 715-881), as when Eden declares himself 'a Heaven-grade genius' (Ep 761).

name: Imogen
reason: A US-origin name, 'Imogen', was assigned to this senior female elder of Cloud Hall; her source counterpart could not be identified from the evidence.
description: Elder Imogen is a Life-and-Death Realm master and the most senior elder of Cloud Hall, outranking Saint Morphens and Emanuel Drew and surpassed only by Tia. She faces down the Heartland King Maddox at Cloud Hall's gates and accompanies the expedition into the Celestial Tomb of Vesper (Eps 716-957).

name: House Dillon
reason: One of Cloudhaven's third-rank families was localized as 'House Dillon'; the source has four such families (Zhuo, Chen, Fei, Wu), and the exact counterpart cannot be pinned down from the evidence.
description: One of the third-rank Legacy Houses of Cloudhaven, alongside House Drew, House Shaw, and House Ward (Ep 722). Larry Dillon, a renowned master of defense, belonged to it; the house backed Emanuel's failed rebellion against Cloud Hall.

name: Vanguard Team
reason: The source team name 'Red Maple Team' (ch 716) was renamed 'Vanguard Team' - in the episode Zane himself proposes the name - to sound more martial in English.
description: The small strike team Zane names in Ep 738 (with Finn, Patrick, and Lewis), sent fourteen hundred miles east of Oracle City to destroy a teleportation array the Corrupted Divine Kingdom was secretly building in Melody City.

name: Yellow Spring
reason: The source's mythological term 'Yellow Spring' (the Chinese underworld river, chs 725-726) was kept as-is.
description: The river of the Netherworld along which the Life and Death Wind blows (Ep 749); part of the lore explaining the deathly wind that strikes Tia.

name: Double Stars Brilliance
reason: The source technique 'Glory of Twin Stars' (ch ~730) was localized as 'Double Stars Brilliance'.
description: A devastating technique of Zane's Stellar Body (part of the Transcendent Divine Might) that summons two blazing stars whose combined light he gathers in his hands; he unleashes it against the Life and Death Wind (Eps 750-752, title of Ep 750).

name: Walter Reed
reason: The character's Chinese name 'Xue Xi' was fully localized to the US-origin name 'Walter Reed', a doctor's name befitting his role as a famous physician.
description: A famous, miracle-working physician of Oracle City (Eps 760-766). He examines the comatose Tia and delivers the grim verdict that her Raw Vitality is almost entirely gone - she is not sick or injured, merely a breath away from death - mirroring Xue Xi's diagnosis of Ning Yudie in the source.

name: House Lee
reason: The source's 'Li Family', a third-grade aristocratic family (ch 744), was localized as 'House Lee', keeping the surname's sound while fitting the show's 'House' convention for Legacy Houses.
description: A fallen aristocratic house (Eps 767-768) that once, seven hundred years ago, saved a master from the Union of Seven Divine Kingdoms; by the present it is 'history', its surviving scion hoping to rebuild.

name: Secret Territories
reason: The source's 'secret realms' inside the Heavenly Feather Saint Ocean were collectively localized as the 'Secret Territories' of the Sacred Feather Sea.
description: The four hidden realms inside the Sacred Feather Sea (Eps 779-782); entry requires belonging to a Martial House of fifth rank or above, and the four kingdoms compete fiercely over access quotas.

name: Deepswallow
reason: An adaptation-coined creature name with no identifiable source counterpart, invented for Western fantasy flavor.
description: A fearsome ocean beast of the crushing depths; a character recalls hunting a young Deepswallow as one of the most dangerous moments of his life (Ep 915).

name: Luo Tianxing
issues: Un-localized pinyin name retained in delivered episodes: 'Luo Tianxing' is the pseudonym Zane uses in the Martial House arc (Eps 786, 791), kept verbatim from the source (Luo Zheng's pseudonym, chs 761+) while every other name in the show is Westernized.
reason: The source pseudonym 'Luo Tianxing', which Luo Zheng invents to hide his identity, was carried over unchanged instead of being localized like all other names.
description: The false name Zane registers under during the Crystal Martial House token trials in the Harlen Divine Kingdom (Eps 786, 791); the Soul Sea masters assess 'Luo Tianxing' as having strength comparable to late-stage Spirit-Tribulation.

name: Feather Emperor
reason: The source title 'Feather Emperor' was kept as-is, since the English term already suits the adaptation.
description: The ancient sovereign of the Sacred Feather Sea lore after whom the Feather Emperor's Secret Realm (and, in the source, Feather Emperor Island) is named (Eps 792-857); his secret land is considered the safest of the hidden realms for those who follow its rules.

name: Divine Emperor’s Secret Realm
reason: The source location 'Divine Emperor Secret Realm' (one of the secret realms of the Heavenly Feather Saint Ocean) was kept nearly verbatim.
description: One of the hidden realms of the Sacred Feather Sea alongside the Feather Emperor's and the Mysterious Dream (Eps 795, 998); in the source it is an extremely dangerous place known for its corpses.

name: Princess Consort
reason: Generic royal title used in passing (cf. source 'Crown Princess'), not a distinct entity.

name: Dragon's Tooth
reason: The source weapon 'Dragon Tooth' (Zhan Yun's saber, ch 779) was kept with a possessive restyling as 'Dragon's Tooth'.
description: Edwin's named saber (Ep 802), announced in his duel against Zane and cracked straight down the blade by Zane's first slash - matching the source scene where Zhan Yun's Dragon Tooth is shattered.

name: Little Monster’
reason: The source epithet 'little monster' (the prodigy-beast of the Nine Cauldron Martial House, secretly the embodiment of the world's will) was kept as the proper name 'Little Monster'.
description: A feral, monstrously talented being treated as a national treasure by the Divine Kingdoms (Eps 814-887). Zane cannot simply be killed after the Little Monster's standoff, and killing the Little Monster's soul is treated as an outrage; in the source it is unknowingly the embodiment of the Great Thousand World's will.

name: Fiona’s Time Law
reason: The source's 'Law of Time' - cultivated by Huo Yuner, localized as Fiona - was rendered 'Time Law' in the adaptation.
description: The rare law Fiona cultivates alongside her other law, letting her slow the flow of time around her (Eps 816-884); Zane impresses the white-haired priest by grasping Fiona's Time Law unusually quickly.

name: Dragons and True Phoenixes
reason: A conjunction of two race generics (dragons; true phoenixes), not a single entity.

name: Sacrificial Ceremony
reason: The source event term 'sacrificial ceremony' (ch ~810) was kept as-is.
description: The rite conducted by the white-haired priest after the duels that opens the Sacred Feather Sea (Eps 836-838); once complete, the warriors of the seven kingdoms receive vials of Dragon Blood and may enter.

name: World's Will
reason: The source concept 'the will of the world' (the Great Thousand World's collective will) was localized as the 'World's Will'.
description: The collective consciousness of the world, which Zane merges with, gaining access to the Memory of the World's Will - a complete record he searches for information such as the White-Haired Priest's origins (Eps 837, 944).

name: Feather Emperor’s Secret Land
issues: Name drift in episodes: the same location is called 'Feather Emperor's Secret Realm' (Ep 792) and 'Feather Emperor's Secret Land' / 'secret lands' (Eps 795, 796, 844, 857-859).
reason: The source location 'Feather Emperor Secret Realm' was localized as the 'Feather Emperor's Secret Land' (with 'Secret Realm' also appearing in some episodes).
description: The best-known hidden realm of the Sacred Feather Sea (Eps 792-859), considered mostly safe for those who follow the rules, which is why the seven kingdoms send their younger generation there; Zane's goal within it is to mine ancient heartstones.

name: Fredrick’s Heavenly Thunder Halberd
reason: The source weapon 'Heavenly Thunder Halberd' (Liu Xiu's one-time-use Semi-Divine tool, chs 840-842; Liu Xiu localized as Fredrick) was kept verbatim.
description: A single-use halberd of Semi-Divine grade owned by Fredrick (Eps 868-869), of immeasurable value in the Divine Kingdoms - a life-saving gift mentioned alongside the Semi-Divine Weapon on Fiona's arm.

name: Five Elements Tribulations
reason: The source term 'Five Elements Tribulation' (ch 858) was kept, pluralized to cover the sequence of elemental tribulations.
description: The sequence of elemental heavenly tribulations - thunder, metal, wind, water, and their kin - that descend one after another during Zane's breakthrough (Eps 880-881).

name: Reincarnation Tribulation
reason: The source term 'Reincarnation Tribulation' (ch 862) was kept as-is.
description: A legendary tribulation of the highest order (Eps 885-886); in the source, Celestial Venerable Ling Xiao opened the Mahayana Lotus Flower only after crossing the Reincarnation Tribulation 2.6 million years ago.

name: Eastern Region
reason: The source region name 'Eastern Region' was kept as-is.
description: The region containing the thirty-three peaks of the sect where Zane trained (Eps 886-887); while redirecting a world-threatening black light through the world's mountains, Zane deliberately excludes the Eastern Region to spare the disciples still cultivating on its slopes.

name: Martin
reason: The character's Chinese name 'Zhou Qing' was fully localized to the US-origin name 'Martin' for the Western setting of the adaptation.
description: One of the Harlen Divine Kingdom's masters (Ep 890), keeper of the soul conduits used to activate Soul Cores; the Emperor orders him to bring out all the spares, to his astonishment - mirroring Zhou Huang's order to Zhou Qing about the Spirit Cages in the source.

name: Orson Garrison
reason: The character's Chinese name 'Gu Heche' was fully localized to the US-origin name 'Orson Garrison'; the surname 'Garrison' was shared with his daughter Dorothea Garrison to keep the family unit consistent (source surname Gu, as in Gu Pei'er).
description: Dorothea Garrison's father, whose name stands in the first row of the Talent Tablet in the Tower of Crystal (Eps 920-924); Zane's casual mention of the name shocks Dorothea and proves he truly entered the lost tower.

name: Plate of Seven Wards
reason: The source treasure 'Seven Star Plate' (Qing Feng's star-linked artifact, ch 908; Qing Feng localized as Delroy) was renamed 'Plate of Seven Wards' to emphasize its seven protective uses.
description: Delroy's precious divine-class defensive treasure (Ep 931), with the catch that it only has seven uses; in the source it connects its bearer to the seven stars.

name: Southern Sky Mountains
reason: An adaptation-named mountain locale; no matching source place name was found in the aligned chapters.
description: A mountain range where Zane killed Simon, to the disbelief of those he later tells (Ep 938).

name: Water Pattern Domain
reason: The source's 'light blue water domain' (Lan Bing's Water Domain, ch ~920; Lan Bing localized as Lacey) was rendered 'Water Pattern Domain'.
description: Lacey's shimmering light-blue defensive domain (Ep 943), which shields her from an Ogre's flames during the attack on the Sanctuary, holding firm even as she is pursued.
